start.text: Back again. Good. I have something for importers. It's optional, and I'd rather you skip it than regret it.
Escrow on delivery. You pay into a smart contract: a rule that lives on the network and holds your money. It pays the supplier when your goods arrive. Not before.
Why would a supplier agree to that?
Because they can see the money is locked. They ship the same day instead of waiting a week for a wire to land.
It costs 0.6 percent, fifteen dollars minimum. If the goods never come, the contract sends your money back. Nobody has to trust anybody's promise.

catch.text: It runs on software, and software has bugs. My contract has been audited twice. I'd still say: don't put more in it than you can live without for a week.
I'll send you the terms. Say yes or no. Both are fine answers.

terms.text: Sending them now. Read the fee twice. I'd rather you trust the number than me.
